outcome_detail: $475,000 settlement; the federal case was dismissed in July 2024 after the parties reached a settlement, and the amount was disclosed in reporting in August-September 2024. The settlement was paid entirely by the city's insurer; the city denied liability.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges against the accused officers were reported in coverage of the case.
description: Teresa Williams, the first female officer in the Iron Mountain Police Department's history, sued the City of Iron Mountain and department officials in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Michigan on February 13, 2023. The suit alleged that Deputy Director Joseph Dumais and Sergeant Garth Budek subjected her to years of sexual harassment and assault, including groping, forced kissing, and coerced oral sex, and that the two made a bet over which officer would have sex with her first after she was hired. The complaint also alleged that Director Ed Mattson and the city ignored her reports and retaliated against her, forcing her resignation in April 2022. The city denied the allegations and any liability. The case was dismissed in July 2024 after a settlement, later disclosed as $475,000, paid entirely by the city's insurer.
